title: ValidationVerdict
description:
STORY-035-12. The output of stampvalidate.ValidateFinal, and the exact stdout shape the agent-stamp-validate CLI prints on exit codes 0 (valid) and 1 (well-formed but policy-invalid) alike. Exit code 2 (malformed input/catalog/tool failure) prints no Verdict at all.

`checks` always carries all eight frozen rules, in this fixed order, regardless of outcome ("every check evaluated; Verdict lists all") - there is no short-circuit and no rule a failure elsewhere skips. `valid` is the AND of every `checks[].passed`; there is no separate bypass field.

valid.description: True iff every entry in `checks` passed. This is the sole authority for whether execution may proceed - a caller must not derive it by re-inspecting individual checks.

checks.description: Exactly the eight frozen rules (STORY-035-12 'Frozen validation rules'), each evaluated unconditionally: approved_pair, forbidden_for, entitlement_permitted, metered_dual_key, placement, catalog_drift_fails_closed, not_expired, override_within_policy.

catalog_version.description: The digest of the catalog ValidateFinal actually loaded and validated against - independent of, and compared against, the stamp's own catalog_version by the catalog_drift_fails_closed check.

name.description: The frozen rule name. Stable: never re-pointed at a different rule.

reason_code.description: Frozen reason-code enumeration (STORY-035-12: 'incl. placement_evidence_expired, catalog_version_stale, stamp_expired, vendor_profile_with_placement, metered_authority_missing' - all five present here, alongside every other code this build can emit). A passed check still carries a reason_code (usually "ok", or a more specific pass-side code such as placed_and_fresh, not_applicable, no_override or override_recorded) so a reader never has to infer why a check passed from its name alone.

message.description: Human-readable explanation naming the deciding facts - read by whoever is debugging a refused launch.

allOf.description: reason_code "ok" is legal only on a passed check - it is a generic pass marker, never a way to report a failure without naming a specific reason.
Every failure-side reason_code implies passed: false - none of these codes describes a passing check.
